subject: Logic
title: Material Biconditional
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Material Biconditional.

hook.text: "You pass if and only if you score above 70." Both directions must hold—not just one.

buildup.text: P ↔ Q means P → Q AND Q → P. Both the conditional and its converse must be true.

discovery.text: P ↔ Q is true when P and Q match (both true or both false). It's false when they disagree.

twist.text: "If and only if" is much stronger than just "if." Dropping "only if" halves the requirement.

climax.text: Definitions in math use biconditionals. "Even" means n = 2k if and only if n is divisible by 2.

quiz.question: When is P ↔ Q true?
options: When P and Q have the same truth value
